messages.subject: Re: TMB does not free memory when use from package
messages.subject_clean: TMB does not free memory when use from package
messages.body_plain:
I have now managed to trace the problem down further with the linreg_parallel example. Essentially, it seems that objects assigned in the body of MakeADFun are sometimes almost never garbage collected. I still trying to figure out why.

Regarding:

> The increase in memory usage is not as large as before but it is still there. I am not sure why this is the case.

Then I am guessing that this is the case since I am passing the same data and parameter object each time. Thus, there is only a single version of these objects regardless of the number of calls to MakeADFun in my previous reply.

Here is the example:

```r

library(TMB)

# very simple example of what we will do
counter <- 0L
set_marker <- function(){
  pf <- parent.frame()
  local({
    # we will now when the parent enviroment is cleaned up
    you_will_know_when_cleaned_up <- environment()
    reg.finalizer(
      you_will_know_when_cleaned_up,
      function(e) {
        .GlobalEnv$counter <- .GlobalEnv$counter + 1L
        message(sprintf("cleaning.... %10d", .GlobalEnv$counter))
      })
  }, envir = pf)
}

dummy_func <- function(a = 1, b = 2){
  a + b
}
trace(dummy_func, expression(set_marker()), at = 1)
#R> [1] "dummy_func"

dummy_func()
#R> [1] Tracing dummy_func() step 1
#R> [1] 3

gc()
#R> cleaning....          1
#R> [1]       used (Mb) gc trigger  (Mb) max used  (Mb)
#R> Ncells 1612025 86.1    2595512 138.7  2595512 138.7
#R> Vcells 3291645 25.2    8388608  64.0  5422640  41.4

# it also works with other functions
trace(mean.default, expression(set_marker()), at = 1)
#R> Tracing function "mean.default" in package "base"
#R> [1] "mean.default"

mean(1:4)
#R> [1] Tracing mean.default(1:4) step 1
#R> [1] 2.5

gc()
#R> cleaning....          2

#R>           used (Mb) gc trigger  (Mb) max used  (Mb)

#R> Ncells 1641385 87.7    2843692 151.9  2843692 151.9
#R> Vcells 3332139 25.5    8388608  64.0  4453005  34.0

# now for the example
setwd(system.file("examples", package = "TMB"))
dyn.load(dynlib("linreg_parallel"))

trace(MakeADFun, expression(set_marker()), at = 1)
#R> Tracing function "MakeADFun" in package "TMB"
#R> [1] "MakeADFun"

set.seed(123)
n <- 100000 # ~ moderate amount of memory allocations
tmp_file <- tempfile() # do not want to see all the printed information
openmp(6)

for(i in 1:1000 - 1L){

  data <- list(Y = rnorm(n) + 1:n, x= 1:n)
  sink(tmp_file)
  parameters <- list(a = 0, b = 0, logSigma = 0)
  func <- MakeADFun(data, parameters, DLL = "linreg_parallel")
  FreeADFun(func)
  sink()
  gc()

  if(i %% 100L == 0)
    print(gc())
  gc()
}
```

The garbage collector only cleans up the environment I assign once in all the 1000 calls I make! This is exactly the behavior I have seen in some of my simulation studies. Unfortunately, the effect is that the method is of little use in a simulation study as one runs out of memory.

Interestingly, the number of garbage collected environments seems to differ from run to run.

messages.subject: Re: TMB does not free memory when use from package
messages.subject_clean: TMB does not free memory when use from package
messages.body_plain:
Sounds very similar to the problems reported in this issue:

https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/issues/316

To summarize the findings:

- The gc() behaviour seems to have changed (to worse) somewhere between R-3.4.4 and R-3.6.2.
- The frequency of full garbage collection seems to interfere with the number of threads (very weird).

Regarding your example, it's surprising that R fails to clean up it's own memory (the data object inside env). Either this is an R problem, in which case it should be possible to make the example independent of TMB. Or it's TMB doing something bad that prevents the data from being collected?

messages.body_plain:
Thank you for the reply! The error seems to be similar to the Github issue.

With some limited testing, everything works fine when I use only one thread (openmp(1)) as also indicated in the Github issue.

> Regarding your example, it's surprising that R fails to clean up it's own memory (the data object inside env). Either this is an R problem, in which case it should be possible to make the example independent of TMB. Or it's TMB doing something bad that prevents the data from being collected?

I would suspect the latter since it seems related to using more threads and as R is single threaded.

For the record if I change the for loop to:

for(i in 1:1000 - 1L){
  data <- list(Y = rnorm(n) + 1:n, x= 1:n)
  sink(tmp_file)
  parameters <- list(a = 0, b = 0, logSigma = 0)
  func <- MakeADFun(data, parameters, DLL = "linreg_parallel")

  sink()
  gc()

  FreeADFun(func)

  if(i %% 100L == 0)
    print(gc())
  gc()
}

Then I only get the `Free parallelADFun object.` messages when the "cleaning.... ##" stops occurring. So only the C++ objects seems be destroyed.

I would suspect that it has to do with some of these lines:
https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/blob/a81ff89f5e65fae801ce0d2634cde575d460ee70/TMB/inst/include/tmb_core.hpp#L1209
https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/blob/a81ff89f5e65fae801ce0d2634cde575d460ee70/TMB/inst/include/tmb_core.hpp#L1127-L1151
There is no issue if we run the example I have with config(tape.parallel = FALSE).

This leaves me with these lines where R is involved (I guess):
https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/blob/a81ff89f5e65fae801ce0d2634cde575d460ee70/TMB/inst/include/tmb_core.hpp#L1131
https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/blob/a81ff89f5e65fae801ce0d2634cde575d460ee70/TMB/inst/include/tmb_core.hpp#L1133
https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/blob/a81ff89f5e65fae801ce0d2634cde575d460ee70/TMB/inst/include/tmb_core.hpp#L1143

By the way, I think that this line: https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/blob/a81ff89f5e65fae801ce0d2634cde575d460ee70/TMB/inst/include/tmb_core.hpp#L1131

Might be called in parallel and evaluating this line which I think can crash R: https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/blob/a81ff89f5e65fae801ce0d2634cde575d460ee70/TMB/inst/include/tmb_core.hpp#L557

This can be avoided with a #pragma omp master (if I am correct).

Moreover, is this call in the constructor thread-safe: https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/blob/a81ff89f5e65fae801ce0d2634cde575d460ee70/TMB/inst/include/tmb_core.hpp#L767

If not, then I guess one could use the copy-constructor for the objective_function class instead with an object which is created by the master thread.

Thank you for the reply! The error seems to be similar to the Github issue.

With some limited testing, everything works fine when I use only one thread (openmp(1)) as also indicated in the Github iss

messages.subject: Re: TMB does not free memory when use from package

messages.body_plain:
"There is no issue if we run the example I have with config(tape.parallel = FALSE)."

This is a very useful observation! I can confirm that the example 2 from github issue 316 is also solved by setting 'config(tape.parallel = FALSE)'.

"I would suspect that it has to do with some of these lines:"

You are right. One must assume that all macros and functions in the R API are NOT thread safe. Obviously TMB is violating this rule. It used to be mostly OK for read only access, but with recent changes in R (ALTREP) this is no longer the case.
On top of all the problematic code you've already pointed out (thanks!), we should not forget all the DATA_ and PARAMETER_ macros which are also accessing R data structures.
I'm convinced this can all be sorted out using 'pragma omp critical' without a significant performance hit, but it's going to be a fairly big change. Meanwhile, I would consider parallel taping as being broken.

> I would suspect the latter since it seems related to using more threads and as R is single threaded.
>
> For the record if I change the for loop to:
>
> for(i in 1:1000 - 1L){
>   data <- list(Y = rnorm(n) + 1:n, x= 1:n)

messages.body_plain:
The problem might be solved on this branch:

https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/tree/thread_gc

Can you try?

On Wednesday, October 14, 2020 at 10:26:52 AM UTC+2 Kasper Kristensen wrote:
> "There is no issue if we run the example I have with config(tape.parallel = FALSE)."
>
> This is a very useful observation! I can confirm that the example 2 from github issue 316 is also solved by setting 'config(tape.parallel = FALSE)'.
>
> "I would suspect that it has to do with some of these lines:"
>
> You are right. One must assume that all macros and functions in the R API are NOT thread safe. Obviously TMB is violating this rule. It used to be mostly OK for read only access, but with recent changes in R (ALTREP) this is no longer the case.
> On top of all the problematic code you've already pointed out (thanks!), we should not forget all the DATA_ and PARAMETER_ macros which are also accessing R data structures.
> I'm convinced this can all be sorted out using 'pragma omp critical' without a significant performance hit, but it's going to be a fairly big change. Meanwhile, I would consider parallel taping as being broken.
>
> On Tuesday, October 13, 2020 at 10:57:32 AM UTC+2 boen...@gmail.com wrote:
> > Thank you for the reply! The error seems to be similar to the Github issue.
> >
> > With some limited testing, everything works fine when I use only one thread (openmp(1)) as also indicated in the Github issue.
> >
> > > Regarding your example, it's surprising that R fails to clean up it's own memory (the data object inside env). Either this is an R problem, in which case it should be possible to make the example independent of TMB. Or it's TMB doing something bad that prevents the data from being collected?
> > I would suspect the latter since it seems related to using more threads and as R is single threaded.
> >
> > For the record if I change the for loop to:
> >
> > for(i in 1:1000 - 1L){
> >   data <- list(Y = rnorm(n) + 1:n, x= 1:n)
> >   sink(tmp_file)
> >   parameters <- list(a = 0, b = 0, logSigma = 0)
> >   func <- MakeADFun(data, parameters, DLL = "linreg_parallel")
> >   sink()
> >   gc()
> >
> >   FreeADFun(func)
> >   if(i %% 100L == 0)
> >     print(gc())
> >   gc()
> > }
> >
> > Then I only get the `Free parallelADFun object.` messages when the "cleaning.... ##" stops occurring. So only the C++ objects seems be destroyed.
> >
> > I would suspect that it has to do with some of these lines:
> > https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/blob/a81ff89f5e65fae801ce0d2634cde575d460ee70/TMB/inst/include/tmb_core.hpp#L1209
> > https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/blob/a81ff89f5e65fae801ce0d2634cde575d460ee70/TMB/inst/include/tmb_core.hpp#L1127-L1151
> > There is no issue if we run the example I have with config(tape.parallel = FALSE).
> >
> > This leaves me with these lines where R is involved (I guess):

messages.subject: Small differences in likelihoods reported by nlminb and TMB report for fixed effects models
messages.subject_clean: Small differences in likelihoods reported by nlminb and TMB report for fixed effects models
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,
 I noticed that the negative log likelihood reported by nlminb and TMB when the negative log-likelihood is output using the report function are slightly different for fixed effects models. TMB's likelihood function from obj$fn(obj$env$last.par.best) matches that reported by nlminb, but both differ from obj$report(obj$env$last.par.best)$nll by usually around 1e-8. I was wondering where the difference was coming from? Appreciate the help. May be informative for some efforts getting a population dynamics model to converge and the potential inclusion of a discontinuous likelihood surface (population can-not go below 0). Attached is an example using slightly modified code from the linreg_parallel example found on github.
Thank you

--
Grant Adams
School of Aquatic Fishery Sciences
University of Washington
https://grantdadams.wordpress.com/

messages.body_plain:
Thanks. I ran

  setwd(d <- tempdir())
  download.file("https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/archive/thread_gc.tar.gz",
                "source.tar.gz")
  untar("source.tar.gz")
  setwd("adcomp-thread_gc")
  system("make install")
  setwd(d)

and added a compile("linreg_parallel.cpp") call then everything seems to work!

Some thoughts though:
In the package I mentioned at the start, I would not expect that the R macros are redefined in this way.
There must be potentially noticeable performance implications of wrapping all the R macros in omp critical due to all the thread communication? Using just one thread to do the taping must be attractive then in many applications?
Some of these function must be thread-safe. Take REAL (see https://github.com/wch/r-source/blob/29a8a567e2dad277117fe995bb3879f5c00e1cf4/src/include/Rinternals.h#L503, https://github.com/wch/r-source/blob/54fbdca9d3fc63437d9e697f442d32732fb4f443/src/include/Rinlinedfuns.h#L116-L140). This should be thread-safe I guess if ALTREP(sexp_object) is a nullptr/false.
You are properly going to, but if you forget then remember to wrap everything in #ifdef _OPENMP #endif.
The `Ts_GetRNGstate` might fail I think. All the critical sections share the same unspecified name but the master section does not. One other critical section may be executed while the master section is being executed. I think that you can add a check for whether the thread number is zero and if so then do the GetRNGstate() call in a critical section.
I was interested in whether it is the ALTREP that caused all the trouble. Thus, I changed the example to:

for(i in 1:1000 - 1L){

  data <- list(Y = rnorm(n) + 1:n, x = rep(0, n))

  sink(tmp_file)
  parameters <- list(a = 0, b = 0, logSigma = 0)
  func <- MakeADFun(data, parameters, DLL = "linreg_parallel")
  FreeADFun(func)
  sink()
  gc()

  if(i %% 20L == 0)
    print(gc())
  gc()
}

Thus, there are no ALTREP objects in data. This does not solve the problem it seems though.

messages.body_plain:
"In the package I mentioned at the start, I would not expect that the R macros are redefined in this way."

I agree that the re-defines should be undone by a suitable "undef.hpp".

"There must be potentially noticeable performance implications of wrapping all the R macros in omp critical due to all the thread communication?"

A typical TMB application has relatively few calls to the R-macros (looking up pointers to data etc.). I wouldn't expect the overhead to be significant but of course I might be wrong...

"Using just one thread to do the taping must be attractive then in many applications?"

Yes, that's what config(tape.parallel=FALSE) does. I'm not sure it's worth the effort to allow parallel taping at all given the trouble described in this post.

"Some of these function must be thread-safe. Take REAL"

We never know how these functions will be implemented in the future: https://stat.ethz.ch/pipermail/r-devel/2020-September/079964.html

"You are properly going to, but if you forget then remember to wrap everything in #ifdef _OPENMP #endif."

Think I already did?

"The `Ts_GetRNGstate` might fail I think."

Yes, good point!

On Friday, October 16, 2020 at 9:09:00 AM UTC+2 boen...@gmail.com wrote:
> Thanks. I ran
>

> Some thoughts though:
> In the package I mentioned at the start, I would not expect that the R macros are redefined in this way.
> There must be potentially noticeable performance implications of wrapping all the R macros in omp critical due to all the thread communication? Using just one thread to do the taping must be attractive then in many applications?
> Some of these function must be thread-safe. Take REAL (see https://github.com/wch/r-source/blob/29a8a567e2dad277117fe995bb3879f5c00e1cf4/src/include/Rinternals.h#L503, https://github.com/wch/r-source/blob/54fbdca9d3fc63437d9e697f442d32732fb4f443/src/include/Rinlinedfuns.h#L116-L140). This should be thread-safe I guess if ALTREP(sexp_object) is a nullptr/false.
> You are properly going to, but if you forget then remember to wrap everything in #ifdef _OPENMP #endif.
> The `Ts_GetRNGstate` might fail I think. All the critical sections share the same unspecified name but the master section does not. One other critical section may be executed while the master section is being executed. I think that you can add a check for whether the thread number is zero and if so then do the GetRNGstate() call in a critical section.
> I was interested in whether it is the ALTREP that caused all the trouble. Thus, I changed the example to:

> for(i in 1:1000 - 1L){

>   sink(tmp_file)

>   func <- MakeADFun(data, parameters, DLL = "linreg_parallel")
>   FreeADFun(func)

>   gc()
>
>   if(i %% 20L == 0)
>     print(gc())
>   gc()
> }

> "There must be potentially noticeable performance implications of wrapping all the R macros in omp critical due to all the thread communication?"

I think depends on the time it currently takes to copy the data relativ to taping the objective function. Consider the asMatrix function: https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/blob/e29830ad6537b3ba368dcc34649ee82eb94f535f/TMB/inst/include/convert.hpp#L113-L125

As a benchmark, I created the following file which can be Rcpp::sourceCpp'ed:

  // [[Rcpp::plugins(openmp)]]
  // [[Rcpp::depends(RcppArmadillo)]]
  #include <RcppArmadillo.h>
  #include <omp.h>

  constexpr int const n_threads = 6L;

  using namespace Rcpp;

  // [[Rcpp::export(rng = false)]]
  arma::mat wo_critical(SEXP x){
    Rcpp::NumericMatrix xmat(x);
    int const m = xmat.nrow(),
              n = xmat.ncol();
    arma::mat out;
    omp_set_num_threads(n_threads);

  #pragma omp parallel for lastprivate(out)
    for(int i = 0; i < n_threads; ++i){
      out.set_size(m, n);
      for(int j = 0; j < n; ++j)
        for(int k = 0; k < m; ++k)
          out[j * m + k] =  REAL(x)[j * m + k];
    }

    return out;
  }

  // [[Rcpp::export(rng = false)]]
  arma::mat w_critical(SEXP x){
    Rcpp::NumericMatrix xmat(x);
    int const m = xmat.nrow(),
              n = xmat.ncol();
    arma::mat out;
    int const n_threads = 6L;
    omp_set_num_threads(n_threads);

  #pragma omp parallel for lastprivate(out)
    for(int i = 0; i < n_threads; ++i){
      out.set_size(m, n);
      for(int j = 0; j < n; ++j)
        for(int k = 0; k < m; ++k)
  #pragma omp critical
          out[j * m + k] = REAL(x)[j * m + k];
    }

    return out;
  }

  /*** R
  n <- 100L
  m <- 10000L
  x <- matrix(rnorm(m * n), m)
  res <- w_critical(x)
  all.equal(x, res)
  res <- wo_critical(x)
  all.equal(x, res)

  bench::mark(w =  w_critical(x), wo =  wo_critical(x), min_time = 2)
  */

This shows a 50 fold increase in computation time.

messages.body_plain:
The asMatrix example is exactly what I had in mind with this FIXME:
https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/blob/thread_gc/TMB/inst/include/thread_safe_R.hpp#L7-L8
It's easy to fix by putting REAL(x) outside the loop.

So, I have the following questions: Assuming that these few obvious
issues are fixed in asMatrix etc, can we expect to see substantial
overhead with parallization due to the 'omp critical' constructs?
And, is the potential gain by parallel taping big enough to justify
the added code complexity?

On Friday, October 16, 2020 at 1:51:59 PM UTC+2 boen...@gmail.com wrote:
> > "There must be potentially noticeable performance implications of wrapping all the R macros in omp critical due to all the thread communication?"
> I think depends on the time it currently takes to copy the data relativ to taping the objective function. Consider the asMatrix function: https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/blob/e29830ad6537b3ba368dcc34649ee82eb94f535f/TMB/inst/include/convert.hpp#L113-L125
>
> As a benchmark, I created the following file which can be Rcpp::sourceCpp'ed:
>
>   // [[Rcpp::plugins(openmp)]]

>   #include <RcppArmadillo.h>
>   #include <omp.h>

>
>   using namespace Rcpp;

>   arma::mat wo_critical(SEXP x){
>     Rcpp::NumericMatrix xmat(x);
>     int const m = xmat.nrow(),
>               n = xmat.ncol();
>     arma::mat out;
>     omp_set_num_threads(n_threads);
>
>   #pragma omp parallel for lastprivate(out)
>     for(int i = 0; i < n_threads; ++i){
>       out.set_size(m, n);
>       for(int j = 0; j < n; ++j)
>         for(int k = 0; k < m; ++k)
>           out[j * m + k] =  REAL(x)[j * m + k];
>     }
>
>     return out;
>   }
>

>     arma::mat out;

>       for(int j = 0; j < n; ++j)
>         for(int k = 0; k < m; ++k)

> This shows a 50 fold increase in computation time.

> > Think I already did?

> The asMatrix example is exactly what I had in mind with this FIXME:
> https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/blob/thread_gc/TMB/inst/include/thread_safe_R.hpp#L7-L8
> It's easy to fix by putting REAL(x) outside the loop.

Argh, right. But I figure one needs to
> ... check ALTREP(sexp_object) is a nullptr/false

first just in case.

> So, I have the following questions: Assuming that these few obvious
> issues are fixed in asMatrix etc, can we expect to see substantial
> overhead with parallization due to the 'omp critical' constructs?
> And, is the potential gain by parallel taping big enough to justify
> the added code complexity?

Tapping does not seem to take much time in the applications I have relative to the minimization. However, it would be nice in applications where this is not true? Though, there may come some issues in the future if R's C code changes.

On Friday, October 16, 2020 at 6:40:03 PM UTC+2 kasper.k...@gmail.com wrote:
> The asMatrix example is exactly what I had in mind with this FIXME:
> https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/blob/thread_gc/TMB/inst/include/thread_safe_R.hpp#L7-L8

>
> So, I have the following questions: Assuming that these few obvious
> issues are fixed in asMatrix etc, can we expect to see substantial
> overhead with parallization due to the 'omp critical' constructs?
> And, is the potential gain by parallel taping big enough to justify
> the added code complexity?
>

messages.body_plain:
> So, I have the following questions: Assuming that these few obvious
> issues are fixed in asMatrix etc, can we expect to see substantial
> overhead with parallization due to the 'omp critical' constructs?

And no, I would not expect a big overhead then!

On Monday, October 19, 2020 at 8:05:33 AM UTC+2 boen...@gmail.com wrote:
> > The asMatrix example is exactly what I had in mind with this FIXME:
> > https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/blob/thread_gc/TMB/inst/include/thread_safe_R.hpp#L7-L8
> > It's easy to fix by putting REAL(x) outside the loop.
> Argh, right. But I figure one needs to
> > ... check ALTREP(sexp_object) is a nullptr/false
>
> first just in case.
>
> > So, I have the following questions: Assuming that these few obvious
> > issues are fixed in asMatrix etc, can we expect to see substantial
> > overhead with parallization due to the 'omp critical' constructs?
> > And, is the potential gain by parallel taping big enough to justify
> > the added code complexity?
> Tapping does not seem to take much time in the applications I have relative to the minimization. However, it would be nice in applications where this is not true? Though, there may come some issues in the future if R's C code changes.
>
> On Friday, October 16, 2020 at 6:40:03 PM UTC+2 kasper.k...@gmail.com wrote:
> > The asMatrix example is exactly what I had in mind with this FIXME:
> > https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/blob/thread_gc/TMB/inst/include/thread_safe_R.hpp#L7-L8
> > It's easy to fix by putting REAL(x) outside the loop.
> >
> > So, I have the following questions: Assuming that these few obvious
> > issues are fixed in asMatrix etc, can we expect to see substantial
> > overhead with parallization due to the 'omp critical' constructs?
> > And, is the potential gain by parallel taping big enough to justify
> > the added code complexity?
> >
> >
> > On Friday, October 16, 2020 at 1:51:59 PM UTC+2 boen...@gmail.com wrote:
> > > > "There must be potentially noticeable performance implications of wrapping all the R macros in omp critical due to all the thread communication?"
> > > I think depends on the time it currently takes to copy the data relativ to taping the objective function. Consider the asMatrix function: https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/blob/e29830ad6537b3ba368dcc34649ee82eb94f535f/TMB/inst/include/convert.hpp#L113-L125
> > >
> > > As a benchmark, I created the following file which can be Rcpp::sourceCpp'ed:
> > >
> > >   // [[Rcpp::plugins(openmp)]]
> > >   // [[Rcpp::depends(RcppArmadillo)]]
> > >   #include <RcppArmadillo.h>
> > >   #include <omp.h>
> > >
> > >   constexpr int const n_threads = 6L;
> > >
> > >   using namespace Rcpp;
> > >
> > >   // [[Rcpp::export(rng = false)]]
> > >   arma::mat wo_critical(SEXP x){
> > >     Rcpp::NumericMatrix xmat(x);
> > >     int const m = xmat.nrow(),
> > >               n = xmat.ncol();
> > >     arma::mat out;
> > >     omp_set_num_threads(n_threads);
> > >
> > >   #pragma omp parallel for lastprivate(out)
> > >     for(int i = 0; i < n_threads; ++i){
> > >       out.set_size(m, n);
> > >       for(int j = 0; j < n; ++j)
> > >         for(int k = 0; k < m; ++k)
> > >           out[j * m + k] =  REAL(x)[j * m + k];
> > >     }
> > >
> > >     return out;
> > >   }
> > >
> > >   // [[Rcpp::export(rng = false)]]
> > >   arma::mat w_critical(SEXP x){
> > >     Rcpp::NumericMatrix xmat(x);
> > >     int const m = xmat.nrow(),
> > >               n = xmat.ncol();
> > >     arma::mat out;
> > >     int const n_threads = 6L;
> > >     omp_set_num_threads(n_threads);
> > >
> > >   #pragma omp parallel for lastprivate(out)
> > >     for(int i = 0; i < n_threads; ++i){
> > >       out.set_size(m, n);
> > >       for(int j = 0; j < n; ++j)
> > >         for(int k = 0; k < m; ++k)
> > >   #pragma omp critical
> > >           out[j * m + k] = REAL(x)[j * m + k];
> > >     }
> > >
> > >     return out;
> > >   }
> > >
> > >   /*** R
> > >   n <- 100L
> > >   m <- 10000L
> > >   x <- matrix(rnorm(m * n), m)
> > >   res <- w_critical(x)
> > >   all.equal(x, res)
> > >   res <- wo_critical(x)
> > >   all.equal(x, res)
> > >
> > >   bench::mark(w =  w_critical(x), wo =  wo_critical(x), min_time = 2)
> > >   */
> > >
> > > This shows a 50 fold increase in computation time.
> > >
> > > > Think I already did?

Take REAL (see https://github.com/wch/r-source/blob/29a8a567e2dad277117fe995bb3879f5c00e1cf4/src/include/Rinternals.h#L503, https://github.com/wch/r-source/blob/54fbdca9d3fc63437d9e697f442d32732fb4f443/src/include/Rinlinedfuns.h#L116-L140). This is an old thread, but I'm curious about using the inverse() syntax here. To clarify, what is the value mat  in lltCovMAT(mat) ?

On Thursday, August 30, 2018 at 8:58:19 PM UTC-7 craig....@gmail.com wrote:
> I have come across some TMB inversion code and general code to incorporate the eigen functionality you just have to incorporate the namespace Eigen:: if any one is interested.
>
>   Eigen::LLT< Matrix<Type, Eigen::Dynamic, Eigen::Dynamic> > lltCovMAT(mat);
>   matrix<Type> LN = lltCovMAT.matrixL();
>   matrix<Type> LinvN = LN.inverse();
>
> Hopefully that might be useful to some newbies like myself.
>
>
>
> On Wednesday, August 29, 2018 at 2:53:07 PM UTC+12, Craig Marsh wrote:
> > Hi there I have 2 questions to the group,
> >
> > Firstly
> > - is C++ 11 compilation flag allowed? I was getting errors saying
> >
> > I get two warnings/errors that I think suggest we don't
> >
> > "'auto' changes meaning in C++11; please remove it"
> >
> > "range-based 'for' loops are not allowed in C++98 mode"
> >
> > that was for a loop structured as
> >
> > for(auto& val : vector_of_values
> >
> > Secondly
> >
> > I am doing inversions and determinants of large-ish matricies, the code I am bringing across used the eigen library like below,
> > Determinant
> >   PartialPivLU<Matrix<double,Dynamic,Dynamic>> lu(M);
> >   auto& LU = lu.matrixLU();
> >   double c = lu.permutationP().determinant(); // -1 or 1
> >
> > and for the inversion
> >
> >   V_invert = Vmat.llt().solve(MatrixXd::Identity(N_bins - 1, N_bins - 1));
> >
> > I went down that road because in the eigen information it says "If your matrix is of a very small fixed size (at most 4x4) this allows Eigen <https://eigen.tuxfamily.org/dox/namespaceEigen.html> to avoid performing a LU decomposition, and instead use formulas that are more efficient on such small matrices."
> > Which I took as if your matrix is bigger than 4x4 don't use the matrix.inverse() or matrix.determinant() and use the decomposition methods.
> >
> > So my question is what is the most efficient/fastest method to calculate inverses and determinants of matrices larger than 4x4 <Type> in TMB?
> >
> > Cheers,
> > Craig
